exposure: Maternal postpartum sleep (sleep duration, sleep disturbance, sleep efficiency)
outcome: Maternal perception of infant temperament (infant negative affectivity, infant orienting/regulation)
cohort: The study included 166 postpartum women with a history of depression.
finding: Maternal sleep disruption (shorter sleep duration, greater sleep disturbance, lower sleep efficiency) was associated with higher infant negative affectivity and lower infant orienting/regulation, with these associations being moderated by maternal depression and anxiety symptoms.
